test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Arjun marks the price of his article 50% more than its cost price. If he sells the article for ₹86,580 after allowing a discount of 26%, then what will be the cost price (in ₹) of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150 units.

**Selling Price (SP)** = 150 × (100 − 26) ÷ 100 = 150 × 0.74 = 111 units.

According to the question, 111 units = 86,580.

1 unit = 86,580 ÷ 111 = 780.

**Cost Price (100 units)** = 100 × 780 = 78,000.

**∴ The correct answer is 78,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup %** = 50%, **Discount %** = 26%, **SP** = 86,580.
Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e96972ebba9cda15212370b2bc99dc0ad883794479ac4093054e753d1425da9.png] 
⇒ Let **CP** be x.
⇒ **MP** = x × (150 ÷ 100) = 1.5x.
⇒ **SP** = 1.5x × (74 ÷ 100) = 1.11x.
⇒ 1.11x = 86,580.
⇒ x = 86,580 ÷ 1.11.
⇒ x = 78,000.

**∴ The correct answer is 78,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This formula is useful when profit percentage is given instead of individual values.

Successive Percentage Change

Net Gain/Loss% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100.</p
